headline: Tarique Rahman calls Nov 7 Bangladesh's Magna Carta
summary: The BNP chief stated that the 1975 events laid the foundation for a shared Bangladeshi identity and national unity during National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
details: BNP chief Tarique Rahman described November 7 as "Bangladesh's Magna Carta," stating that the 1975 events established the foundation for a shared national identity and unity.
Speaking at the Army Stadium in Dhaka Cantonment, he emphasized that regardless of religion or ethnicity, all citizens share a single identity as Bangladeshis.
Tarique and his wife Zubaida Rahman watched performances by the National Cadet Corps and Scouts depicting the Liberation War, the events of Nov 7, and the 2024 mass uprising.
He urged the younger generation to view history as a source of inspiration for self-respect and the building of a prosperous future.
The BNP chief called for national unity to prevent any attempt to undermine the country's sovereignty or democratic rights, pledging that Bangladesh will not be a subservient state.
Tarique drew parallels between the 1971 Liberation War, the 1975 events, and the 2024 mass uprising, stating that while 1971 was for independence, 2024 was to protect it.
He noted that forces defeated in 1975 were later restored to power and established a "fascist rule" before being defeated again in the 2024 uprising.
The BNP observes Nov 7 as National Revolution and Solidarity Day, commemorating the counter-coup that freed Ziaur Rahman from house arrest.
He concluded by stressing that national interests must come first, stating, "Not Delhi, not Pindi, not any other country -- Bangladesh comes first."
caption:
“Not Delhi, not Pindi, not any other country -- Bangladesh comes first.”

BNP chief Tarique Rahman described November 7 as "Bangladesh's Magna Carta," stating that the 1975 events established the foundation for a shared national identity and unity.

Speaking at the Army Stadium in Dhaka Cantonment, he emphasized that regardless of religion or ethnicity, all citizens share a single identity as Bangladeshis.

Tarique and his wife Zubaida Rahman watched performances by the National Cadet Corps and Scouts depicting the Liberation War, the events of Nov 7, and the 2024 mass uprising.

He urged the younger generation to view history as a source of inspiration for self-respect and the building of a prosperous future.

The BNP chief called for national unity to prevent any attempt to undermine the country's sovereignty or democratic rights, pledging that Bangladesh will not be a subservient state.

Tarique drew parallels between the 1971 Liberation War, the 1975 events, and the 2024 mass uprising, stating that while 1971 was for independence, 2024 was to protect it.

He noted that forces defeated in 1975 were later restored to power and established a "fascist rule" before being defeated again in the 2024 uprising.

The BNP observes Nov 7 as National Revolution and Solidarity Day, commemorating the counter-coup that freed Ziaur Rahman from house arrest.

He concluded by stressing that national interests must come first, stating, "Not Delhi, not Pindi, not any other country -- Bangladesh comes first."

headline: 229 wickets in 64 Tests: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket
summary: The Indian pacer announced his retirement on the anniversary of his debut, stating he will continue to play white-ball cricket.
details: Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, ending a 13-year journey that began on November 6, 2013. He shared the news via a video post on Instagram on the anniversary of his Test debut.
caption:
